mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes and preemptively discount future cash flows, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 2% inflation baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% signals wage stickiness and increased labor market tightness, which reduces discount rates and increases expected equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 0.5% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with PAYEMS > 0.5% acceleration, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-acceleration periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST retail sales exceeding 3% from the prior month indicates strengthening consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During triggered months, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) after controlling for lagged SPX and macro variables.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 90 signals supply-side contraction, raising uncertainty and compressing discount rates, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 90 index points in the current month
failure_condition: During INDPRO < 90 events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) after adjusting for macro risk factors.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS rates over a 3-month rolling window reduces the real discount rate applied to equities, amplifying the present value of future cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the easing window, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during a comparable neutral FEDFUNDS regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE above 6% indicates widespread labor market disorganization and wage rigidity, which increases uncertainty and compresses discount rates, tending to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases above 6% in the current month
failure_condition: During UNRATE > 6% events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) after controlling for sector-specific volatility.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS retail sales falling by more than 4% signals a demand contraction, lowering earnings expectations and increasing discounting, which tends to drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases > 4% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During triggered RSAFS declines, 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) after adjusting for sector-specific shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO falls below 90 and GDPC1 (real GDP) lags its prior quarter by more than 2%, it indicates simultaneous supply contraction and weak demand, amplifying discounting effects and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 AND GDPC1 growth < -2% qoq in current quarter
failure_condition: During co-occurrence of INDPRO < 90 and GDPC1 qoq miss, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) after controlling for macro risk factors.
